readerTitle: The agency that grew 20% and kept less money
caseNote: 가상 사례 (12명 규모 디자인 에이전시, 냉난방 설비 업체) + 실제 기업 (Handelsbanken의 예산 폐지, 일반적 서술만)
insight: 예산은 내년에 쓸 돈을 맞히는 예측이 아니라, 압박이 없을 때 미리 내려 두는 우선순위 결정이다.
misconception: 예산은 회계용으로 내년 지출을 추정해 두는 숫자표일 뿐이고, 하나하나 합리적인 지출을 승인하면 전체도 합리적이다.

sources.text: 관리회계의 표준 개념 (예산 편성, 예산과 예측의 구분)
Wallander, J. (1999). Budgeting — an unnecessary evil. Scandinavian Journal of Management.
에이전시와 설비 업체의 모든 수치는 설명용 가상 예시

factChecks.note: 에이전시 계산: 작년 이익 $120k + 매출 증가 $200k − 새 지출 $290k = $30k. 새 지출 $95k + $80k + $45k + $30k + $40k = $290k. 그 밖의 비용은 변하지 않았다고 단순화했습니다.
예산 예시: 목표 매출 $1.3M − 남길 이익 $150k = 쓸 수 있는 돈 $1.15M. 단순 계산을 다시 확인하세요.
Handelsbanken: Jan Wallander가 1970년대 초 CEO로 취임한 뒤 전통적 연간 예산을 없앴다는 내용은 Wallander의 글과 Beyond Budgeting 관련 자료에 나옵니다. 게시 전 연도와 표현을 1차 자료로 다시 확인하세요. 카드에는 '1970s'로만 적었습니다.
설비 업체: 연간 마케팅 예산 $24k 중 7월까지 $20k 사용. 매출이 계획보다 앞서 있다는 설정은 가상입니다.

cards.title: The agency that grew 20% and kept less money
body: A 12-person design agency had its best sales year ever. Revenue rose from $1.0M to $1.2M.
Profit fell from $120k to $30k. Nobody had made a bad decision. That was the problem.

image.label: Rising revenue bar next to a shrinking profit bar
image.brief: 3D 클레이 스타일. 작은 디자인 스튜디오 책상 위에 매출 막대(위로 성장)와 이익 막대(쪼그라듦)가 나란히 서 있다. 대표가 두 막대를 보며 머리를 긁는 모습. 실제 로고 없음.

cards.title: How would you stop this happening again?
body: During the year, requests arrived one at a time: a senior hire, freelancers for a rush, new software, a nicer office. Each one made sense when it was asked for.
The owner wants next year to end differently. What's the best fix?

options.text: The owner personally approves every expense over $500
options.feedback: You gain control but become a bottleneck. And you're still judging each request alone, which is how this year went wrong.

options.text: Before the year starts, decide the profit to keep and how much each area may spend
options.feedback: You trade some flexibility for a clear limit set in advance. Every request can then be weighed against the others, not just on its own.
Quick and easy to explain. But a flat cut hits useful and wasteful spending equally, and it doesn't say what the business is trying to achieve.

cards.title: Five reasonable yeses.
body: Revenue added $200k. The yeses added $290k. Profit: $120k + $200k − $290k = **$30k**.

cards.title: Budgets
body: A **budget** is a plan, made before a period starts, that sets how much the business intends to earn and spend, by category, to reach a goal.
The key word is *intends*. A budget isn't a guess about the future. It's a set of **decisions made in advance**, while you're calm and can see every option side by side.

image.label: Spending requests laid out side by side on one table
image.brief: 인포그래픽. 왼쪽은 요청 카드가 한 장씩 시간 순서로 떨어지는 모습(1월, 4월, 8월). 오른쪽은 같은 카드들이 한 테이블 위에 나란히 놓이고 위에 'Room to spend: $1.15M' 라벨. 오른쪽을 더 밝게.

cards.title: Start from what you want to keep.
body: Next year, the agency plans backward:
list: **Split it:** staff, freelancers, tools, travel, office
cards.callout: The argument happens once, in January. In July, the question is simply: does this fit, and if not, what gives?
cards.softwareNote: For a startup spending investor money, the budget often starts from runway instead of profit: how many months the cash must last. The same logic applies. Decide the limit first, then fit the hires and tools inside it.

cards.title: A bakery, a plumber, a marketing team.
body: A bakery budgets flour, staff hours and one new oven. A plumbing firm budgets vans, training and ads. A marketing team inside a large company gets a budget and must choose between events and online ads.
The size changes. The job doesn't: a budget forces you to rank wants against each other before money is gone, instead of discovering the total at year end.

cards.title: Budgets can create their own bad habits.
body: Teams that fear losing unspent money rush to spend it in December. Managers set easy targets so they look good. A plan set in January can be wrong by March.

Sweden's Handelsbanken dropped traditional annual budgets in the 1970s and relied on other controls instead. The lesson isn't that budgets are bad. It's that a budget is a tool for good decisions, not a goal in itself.

cards.title: Now it's a heating and cooling company.
body: Your firm installs and repairs heating systems. The year's marketing budget was $24k. By July you've spent $20k, because online ads are bringing in profitable jobs. Sales are ahead of plan.
Your office manager says to pause the ads until January. What do you do?

options.text: Pause the ads. A budget is a budget
options.feedback: You protect the plan but switch off a channel that's making money. Following the number can defeat the goal it was set for.

options.text: Decide openly to raise marketing, funded by the extra sales or a cut elsewhere
options.feedback: You keep the working ads and the budget stays a real decision. Changing it on purpose is different from drifting past it.

options.text: Keep running the ads and sort out the numbers at year end
options.feedback: The ads keep working, but you're back to one yes at a time. That's how the agency lost its profit.

cards.title: A budget is a decision, made before the pressure arrives.
body: Decide what you want to keep, then choose what to spend on with all the options in front of you.
**Try it today:** write down the profit you want to keep next quarter. Subtract it from expected revenue. Is your planned spending inside that number?
